newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent firms again, but lacks momentum.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent firms again, but lacks momentum.

text.p: The North Sea wet Brent market crept higher again on Thursday but the market appeared to have peaked with sellers shaving a few cents from offers late in the day.

A wet Brent cargo loading August 7-9 traded two cents firmer at August Brent +17 cents, building on this week's steady rally in Dated differentials. A European major dropped its offer for an August 6-8 stem from August +20 cents to +17 cents.
Another cargo nominated from the paper chains was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline.
Sellers were trying to profit from the continued absence of Iraqi barrels and the tightness of the European crude market, but buyers were trying to keep a lid on gains.
"It's a little bit stronger again, but it seems like its running out of steam...people aren't in the mood for a rampant rally in differentials," said one trader.

Other North sea grades were traded below last done levels. An Ekofisk loading August 11-13 traded at Dated Brent +21 cents, while an August 4-6 Statfjord changed hands at Dated Brent +27 cents on a late pricing basis, equivalent to around Dated Brent +21 cents.
Some traders said that efforts to make trans-Atlantic sales despite a narrow arbitrage on paper, were related to efforts to left Brent values to boost profits on paper positions.
"The real trans-Atlantic market is not transparent to outsiders," said one player. "There is uncertainty as to what game is being played and some market manipulation."
Brent was offered at parity to September WTI for September 5-10 delivery, with later arrivals offered at a 5-15 cent discount.
Prospective Brent buyers in the U.S. were cool to the offers so far but little alternative light, sweet crude was seen available in the early September timeframe.

Brent intermonth spreads firmed slightly on Thursday with August/September done at a high of +18 cents. But CFDS were little changed with next week (July 28-Aug 1) valued at September Brent +7/+11 cents for most of the day.
September Brent was trading three cents down at $18.36 a barrel at 1740 GMT.
